new_statements.quote: La regla de la pronunciación de palabras cubeas es que el acento principal de palabras cubeos ocurre en una de las cuatro primeras sílabas. La segunda sílaba tiene el acento principal en la mayoría de las palabras. Por eso, solamente se indica el acento principal por medio de un acento escrito agudo, como se usa en el español, en las palabras que tienen el acento principal en la primera, la tercera o la cuarta sílaba. Algunas palabras que se escriben igual se diferencian en la pronunciación porque en una la tercera sílaba tiene un acento secundario y en la otra no
new_statements.translation: The pronunciation rule for Cubeo words is that the main stress of Cubeo words occurs on one of the first four syllables. The second syllable carries the main stress in most words. For that reason the main stress is marked, with a written acute accent as used in Spanish, only in words whose main stress is on the first, third or fourth syllable. Some words that are written the same differ in pronunciation because in one the third syllable carries a secondary stress and in the other it does not

new_statements.relation_note: The catalog record for Cubeo (qs-tier-2026-09-12) has an empty rule and there are no existing statements, so there is nothing to agree or disagree with; this work supplies the first rule statement: lexically placed main stress within the first four syllables, second syllable by default, with a contrastive secondary stress. downloaded through the the Internet Archive (2015-04-18 captures of the five SIL Colombia PDF parts at www-01.sil.org/americas/colombia/pubs/), because the listed abstract page and the SIL originals are now 404. The PDF text uses a shifted font encoding (decoded copies. spaces and digits are lost in the layer), so the quote was verified against the rendered page scan.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress is lexically placed within a window of the first four syllables of the word; the second syllable is the default (most words), and words stressed on syllables 1, 3 or 4 are marked with an acute accent in the orthography. Morphology shifts it: the plural suffix -a/-ã takes the main stress when added to a disyllabic word (p. 8: 'El sufijo plural tiene el acento principal si se agrega a una palabra de dos sílabas', cobe 'hueco' vs cobeá 'huecos'); polysyllabic classifiers 'con acento propio' carry their own stress (p. 8); monosyllabic possessive prefixes generally carry the main stress, disyllabic ones are stressed on their second syllable (p. 427). No mention of tone anywhere in the introduction.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Yes: a secondary stress on the third syllable can distinguish homographs, e.g. doreyʉ 'picar' vs doreyʉ 'hormiga no comestible que pica con la cola', both with main stress on the second syllable, written doréyʉ vs doréyʉ́ in the entries (p. 3).
new_statements.exceptions: Dialectal/alternative forms may differ only in the position of main stress (p. 4: caivayʉ vs caiyóvayʉ; macacámidʉ vs mãcacámidʉ, 'la diferencia es del acento principal'); p. 427 lists kinship nouns (mamico, mamicʉ, márepaco, paco, pacʉ, páramoco, parĩmo..) whose 1sg/2sg possessive prefixes do not take the main stress.
new_statements.identity_note: The dictionary covers Cubeo as spoken on the Vaupés, Cuduyarí and Querarí rivers (three dialects marked V, C, Q; the introduction calls their differences minor) and its stress statement is not dialect-specific; alternative forms across dialects may differ only in main-stress position. Work 1 (archive.org rosettaproject_cui_ortho-1) is about Cuiva (Guahiban, cui), not Cubeo.

new_statements.relation_note: Same type as the catalog record (Morse & Maxwell 2000: accent contrastive, on one of the first four syllables, most often the second) and as the statement held by the project from the Salser, Morse & Salser 1999 dictionary ('La segunda sílaba tiene el acento principal en la mayoría de las palabras.. solamente se indica el acento.. en las palabras que tienen el acento principal en la primera, la tercera o la cuarta sílaba'): an earlier (1977) statement of the same second-syllable-default, mark-elsewhere convention. It adds no tonal analysis (Morse & Maxwell and Chacón tie the accent to the first high tone), so it neither refines nor contradicts.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Orthographic convention of the Salsers' Cubeo alphabet: word stress is written with an accent mark /'/ only where it is not on the second syllable; unmarked words are stressed on the second syllable. I.e. second-syllable stress is the default and other positions must be marked word by word (stress position is lexical, with a strong peninitial default). The examples in the chapter carry such marks, e.g. the discourse particles 'cari and 'jacu (barred u) with marked initial stress. Nothing is said about tone. (The 27-letter list in the footnote is garbled in scanned and elided in the quote; /d/ and /u/ in the quote are the barred letters.)
new_statements.exceptions: none beyond the marking convention itself (words not stressed on the second syllable carry a written accent)

tone_statements.quote: This paper explores the realization of stress in Kubeo, a Tukanoan language from the Northwest Amazonia with both stress and tone (H vs. HL). The first H tone of a word docks on the primary stressed syllable, which by default is the second syllable except in words with lexical initial stress. ... In post-tonic unstressed syllables, duration, intensity, and vowel quality are all dependent on lexical tone. Secondary stress is less salient due to interference from lexical tones ...
tone_statements.summary: Two lexical tone patterns, H vs HL, coexist with word stress; the word's first H docks on the primary-stressed syllable (default second syllable, else lexical initial stress): tone choice lexical, alignment follows stress. HL contour vs level sequence, TBU, downstep: not said.

tone_statements.citation: Chacon, Thiago Costa. 2009. Estrutura métrica em Kubêo. ReVEL (Revista Virtual de Estudos da Linguagem), edição especial n. 3: 22 pp. ISSN 1678-8931.
tone_statements.quote: Existem dois tipos de melodias tonais em Kubêo. Uma melodia marcada lexicalmente, que sempre cria espalhamento de tom alto da esquerda para a direita. Chamemos esta melodia de A’. Uma segunda melodia tonal, chamada de A, não é marcada lexicalmente e somente ocorre como default, i.e como resultado de regras fonéticas do acento que sempre marcam com tom alto sílabas acentuadas. Apesar de A e A’ apresentarem um mesmo nível de freqüência fundamental em sílabas acentuadas, as duas melodias contrastam em sílabas subseqüentes à direita, que são geralmente silabas não-acentuadas. Isso é um padrão de contraste tonal raro em línguas [+tonal][+acentual].
tone_statements.translation: There are two types of tonal melodies in Kubeo. One lexically marked melody, which always creates spreading of high tone from left to right; let us call this melody A'. A second tonal melody, called A, is not lexically marked and only occurs as a default, i.e. as the result of phonetic rules of stress that always mark stressed syllables with high tone. Although A and A' show the same fundamental-frequency level on stressed syllables, the two melodies contrast on the subsequent syllables to the right, which are generally unstressed syllables. This is a pattern of tonal contrast that is rare in [+tonal][+stress] languages.

readall_conflicts: Among the listed works there is no disagreement, because only one of them (the 1999 dictionary) was opened and is about Cubeo. One tension is worth recording against material already held by the project from the 2026-09-16 pass (not in this work list): the dictionary says main stress falls on one of the first four syllables (second by default; acute marks stress on the 1st, 3rd or 4th), whereas Chacon (2011) says stress can fall only on the first or second syllable from the left, never later, with the second syllable as the default and first-syllable stress lexically specified, and that stress is not quantity-sensitive. The two agree on the second-syllable default and on lexical marking; they differ on whether stress can sit on syllables 3-4. The dictionary's third/fourth-syllable cases include stressed suffixes and classifiers (plural -á on disyllabic nouns, classifiers 'con acento propio', disyllabic possessive prefixes), so the difference may lie in the word domain and in Chacon's treatment of later prominences as tone or secondary stress rather than in the data; this was not resolved here.

sources.quote: La regla de la pronunciación de palabras cubeas es que el acento principal de palabras cubeos ocurre en una de las cuatro primeras sílabas. La segunda sílaba tiene el acento principal en la mayoría de las palabras. Por eso, solamente se indica el acento principal por medio de un acento escrito agudo, como se usa en el español, en las palabras que tienen el acento principal en la primera, la tercera o la cuarta sílaba. Algunas palabras que se escriben igual se diferencian en la pronunciación porque en una la tercera sílaba tiene un acento secundario y en la otra no

sources.citation: Gordon, Matthew K., Thiago C. Chacon, Kaveh Varjoy & Jullie A. Ferreira. 2016. Acoustic properties of stress in Kubeo. Journal of the Acoustical Society of America 140(4, Supplement): 3396 [172nd ASA meeting abstract]. doi:10.1121/1.4970883.
sources.quote: This paper explores the realization of stress in Kubeo, a Tukanoan language from the Northwest Amazonia with both stress and tone (H vs. HL). The first H tone of a word docks on the primary stressed syllable, which by default is the second syllable except in words with lexical initial stress. ... In post-tonic unstressed syllables, duration, intensity, and vowel quality are all dependent on lexical tone. Secondary stress is less salient due to interference from lexical tones ...
sources.note: Two lexical tone patterns, H vs HL, coexist with word stress; the word's first H docks on the primary-stressed syllable (default second syllable, else lexical initial stress): tone choice lexical, alignment follows stress. HL contour vs level sequence, TBU, downstep: not said.
sources.venue: Journal of the Acoustical Society of America

sources.citation: Chacon, Thiago Costa. 2009. Estrutura métrica em Kubêo. ReVEL (Revista Virtual de Estudos da Linguagem), edição especial n. 3: 22 pp. ISSN 1678-8931.
sources.quote: Existem dois tipos de melodias tonais em Kubêo. Uma melodia marcada lexicalmente, que sempre cria espalhamento de tom alto da esquerda para a direita. Chamemos esta melodia de A’. Uma segunda melodia tonal, chamada de A, não é marcada lexicalmente e somente ocorre como default, i.e como resultado de regras fonéticas do acento que sempre marcam com tom alto sílabas acentuadas. Apesar de A e A’ apresentarem um mesmo nível de freqüência fundamental em sílabas acentuadas, as duas melodias contrastam em sílabas subseqüentes à direita, que são geralmente silabas não-acentuadas. Isso é um padrão de contraste tonal raro em línguas [+tonal][+acentual].
sources.locator: §3.3 'Algumas considerações sobre tom e acento', pp. 14-15
sources.note: Kubeo is classed [+tone][+stress] (Hyman 2006 typology): tone and stress are independent in underlying lexical structure but interact in derivation. Both tone and stress are assigned per syllable (TBU = syllable, not mora). Two tonal melodies: a lexically marked melody A' that spreads high tone rightward, and an unmarked default melody A (high on the stressed syllable only, from phonetic stress rules); they are identical on the stressed syllable and contrast only on the following (unstressed) syllables - an atypical tonal contrast restricted to unstressed syllables; surface patterns A'A-A, AB…

tone.translation: There are two types of tonal melodies in Kubeo. One lexically marked melody, which always creates spreading of high tone from left to right; let us call this melody A'. A second tonal melody, called A, is not lexically marked and only occurs as a default, i.e. as the result of phonetic rules of stress that always mark stressed syllables with high tone. Although A and A' show the same fundamental-frequency level on stressed syllables, the two melodies contrast on the subsequent syllables to the right, which are generally unstressed syllables. This is a pattern of tonal contrast that is rare in [+tonal][+stress] languages.
